How the difference between two meters varies with power

Source: R/agreement.R
agreement_by_level.Rd

Meters often agree at endurance pace and diverge at threshold or in sprints, which a single average difference hides entirely. Seconds are binned by the mean of the two readings rather than by either one of them: binning on one meter and then plotting its own difference against that bin makes measurement noise look like a real trend.

Usage

agreement_by_level(
  aligned,
  width = 25,
  min_seconds = 30,
  min_power = 0,
  block = 60,
  replicates = 500
)

Arguments

aligned

Result of align_rides().

width

Bin width in watts.

min_seconds

Bins with fewer paired seconds than this are dropped.

min_power

Both sources must exceed this to count, in watts.

block

Bootstrap block length in seconds.

replicates

Number of bootstrap replicates. Lower than elsewhere in the package because every band is resampled separately, so 500 across eight bands is already more work than 1000 over the ride as a whole.

Value

A tibble with one row per bin per source pair per run:

run, source_a, source_b

As power_agreement().

band, band_range

Bin centre in watts, and its label. Seconds are binned on the mean of the two meters, never on either one.

seconds, mean_power

Paired seconds in the bin, and their mean level.

bias_w, bias_lo, bias_hi

Mean difference in watts within the bin, with its 95% bootstrap interval.

gain_pc, gain_lo, gain_hi

The same as a percentage.

Seconds dropped for thin bins are carried on the dropped_seconds attribute.

Details

Time is not spread evenly across the power range, so seconds is carried through on every row. Bins thinner than min_seconds are dropped, and how many seconds that discarded is reported as an attribute.

See also

Other agreement: level_dependence(), power_agreement()

Examples

aligned <- read_rides(demo_rides()) |> align_rides()
agreement_by_level(aligned)
